item.title: Arista warns of actively exploited CVSS 10.0 VeloCloud Orchestrator zero day vulnerability CVE-2026-93952
item.cd:description:
Emergency advisories published by SD-WAN platform maintainers warn of active wild exploitation targeting central network orchestrators. Remote unauthenticated adversaries leverage broken authorization validation routines to escalate internal privileges and control software-defined WAN Edge devices.
The zero day vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-93952 with a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, affects on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator VCO servers configured to authenticate Edge devices using certificates. An unauthenticated remote attacker can transmit malformed API calls to bypass internal access controls, executing privileged management functions on the orchestrator host. Compromising the central VCO server grants adversaries remote management access over all connected SD-WAN Edge appliances across enterprise subnets.
Subverting central SD-WAN management orchestrators destroys WAN perimeter boundaries across multi-site enterprises. Because VeloCloud Orchestrators govern site-to-site VPN tunnels, routing policies, and traffic inspection rules, an unauthenticated orchestrator compromise permits threat actors to capture cross-site transit traffic and pivot directly into remote branch networks.
- Apply emergency patched release builds published by Arista across all on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator servers immediately. - Restrict public network exposure of VeloCloud Orchestrator management web interfaces by placing servers on isolated management VLANs. - Inspect VCO system audit logs for unverified API administrative actions or anomalous certificate authentication requests. - Rotate administrative service credentials and device authentication certificates across managed SD-WAN environments.
Software-defined WAN platform security demands strict control plane isolation and rapid zero-day patch execution to ensure central network orchestrators remain insulated from unauthenticated remote takeover. #CodeDefence #Arista #VeloCloud #SDWAN #ZeroDay #RCE #NetworkSecurity #AppSec

item.title: CISA adds ZyXEL GS1900 switch buffer overflow CVE-2026-7273 to KEV catalog following Chinese state hacker attacks
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity authorities have issued an emergency update to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, ordering priority remediation for an unauthenticated switch vulnerability actively weaponized in global espionage campaigns. Chinese state-linked threat actors leverage stack-based buffer overflows to siphon network topologies and hashed root credentials.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-7273, affects ZyXEL GS1900 Smart Managed Switches running firmware 2.90 and earlier. Unauthenticated remote actors transmit malformed HTTP requests to trigger buffer overflows, executing operating system commands with root privileges. Threat intelligence reports confirm a Chinese-speaking threat actor compromised nearly 1,000 devices across 48 countries, using obfuscated Python scripts to exfiltrate hashed credentials and network configurations. CISA mandated federal agency compliance under Binding Operational Directive 26-04 with a September 24 remediation deadline.
Subverting managed network switches compromises hardware switching fabric across corporate branch offices. Because managed switches control local VLAN routing, port security, and network transit streams, an unauthenticated root takeover allows adversaries to intercept local traffic and establish persistent footholds on local network segments.
- Force immediate firmware upgrades across all ZyXEL GS1900 series switches to current patched maintenance releases. - Change default administrative credentials immediately across all deployed network switches and management interfaces. - Restrict web management HTTP routing to switches by enforcing dedicated, non-routable management VLANs. - Perform forensic compromise audits across network switch configurations and inspect for unauthorized configuration changes.
Network switching fabric security relies on strict management plane microsegmentation and immediate firmware patch deployment to ensure hardware switches remain protected from unauthenticated remote command execution. #CodeDefence #ZyXEL #Switching #BufferOverflow #CISA #KEV #NetworkSecurity #HardwareSecurity #Espionage

item.title: Active wild exploitation targets Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows local privilege escalation flaw CVE-2026-32996
item.description:
Cyber threat response labs have issued alerts confirming active wild exploitation targeting a local privilege escalation vulnerability in widely deployed backup agent software. Local unprivileged users exploit memory validation errors to obtain root SYSTEM privileges on Windows endpoints.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-32996, impacts Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows installations. The flaw stems from improper memory validation within local backup service RPC subroutines. An unprivileged local attacker or compromised endpoint process can issue malformed service requests to escalate local execution privileges to SYSTEM level, gaining complete administrative control over host operating systems and local disaster recovery repositories. Threat reports urge immediate prioritization across shared workstations and admin endpoints.
Subverting local backup agents undermines host security isolation and disaster recovery resilience. Possessing SYSTEM privileges obtained via backup daemon subversion permits threat actors to unhook endpoint detection drivers, disable local security logging, and wipe local volume shadow copies prior to deploying secondary ransomware payloads.
- Upgrade Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows installations to release version 13.0.2.29 or higher immediately. - Restrict unprivileged local interactive user rights on shared workstations and server endpoints. - Inspect local system process creation trees and Windows Event Logs for anomalous privilege escalation calls from Veeam services. - Ensure disaster recovery backups are stored in air-gapped, immutable repositories isolated from local endpoint administrative accounts.
Endpoint backup agent defense depends on strict local RPC validation and rapid patch deployment to guarantee disaster recovery services remain insulated from unprivileged local privilege escalation. #CodeDefence #Veeam #BackupSecurity #PrivilegeEscalation #SYSTEM #EndpointSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement
